mainTopic: The end of the rule about cutting down trees (בל תשחית) with two stories about palms growing among vines, then the start of the משנה teaching that paying damages is not enough: the one who caused harm must also ask forgiveness, and the victim should not be cruel.
overview: This עמוד finishes the rule about cutting down trees. The word ״רק״ teaches that value matters, and שמואל and רב חסדא each had date palms cut down to protect more valuable grapevines. Then a new משנה teaches that someone who injures another person must ask forgiveness even after paying, and that a victim who refuses to forgive is cruel. Both lessons come from the story of אברהם and אבימלך. The משנה also rules on permission to cause damage. Injury to the body is always paid for. Damage to property is free only with a clear exemption. Permission given by a third person never helps. The גמרא then explains פסוקים from the אבימלך story, including the lesson that a בן נח is punished for failing to learn. Finally, רבא asks רבה בר מרי for sources of several well-known sayings, and the last one continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Value can override the order of which tree to cut
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the usual order of cutting trees applies even when the tree that would normally be cut is worth more. The word ״רק״ teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the rule applies even when the tree is worth more money. The verse says ״רק״ ("only") to teach an exception.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about which tree to cut down first. It uses the word ״רק״ in the פסוק to show that monetary value can change the usual rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had said that a barren tree is cut down before a fruit tree. Here it asks whether that holds even when the barren tree is worth more. The word ״רק״ limits the rule, so value is taken into account. The same idea means a fruit tree may be cut if it is worth more as wood than for its fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might have thought": introduces a possible but wrong idea
"The verse teaches": brings the source that settles the question
"Only": a limiting word in the פסוק that teaches an exception

phrases.english: One might think: even if it is worth more money?
phrases.notes: He means: what if the barren tree is worth more money than the fruit tree?

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Only."
phrases.notes: דברים 20:20

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ מְעוּלֶּה בְּדָמִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא about cutting trees that began on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The usual order of cutting trees does not apply when value points the other way. The word ״רק״ teaches that value matters.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the two stories that follow, where a more valuable plant is protected by cutting down a less valuable one.

steps.title: שמואל tastes wine in his dates
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tasted wine in dates that grew among grapevines. He realized the palms were weakening the vines, so he had the palms cut down.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's sharecropper brought him dates. He ate them and tasted wine in them. He asked what this was, and was told the palms grow among the vines. שמואל said: "They weaken the vines that much? Tomorrow, bring me their core."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that puts the rule into practice. שמואל ordered date palms cut down because they were draining the more valuable grapevines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The taste of wine in the dates showed that the palms were drawing strength from the vines. Since the vines were worth more, he chose to cut the palms. "Bring me their core" is his way of saying "cut them down."

keyTerms.meaning: A sharecropper who works the field for a share of the crop
The soft edible core of a palm tree

phrases.english: Shmuel's sharecropper brought him dates.
He ate, and tasted in them the taste of wine.
He said to him: What is this?
He said to him: They stand among the grapevines.
He said: They weaken the wine this much?
phrases.notes: "The wine" here means the grapevines themselves.

phrases.english: Tomorrow, bring me from their core.
phrases.notes: You can only get the core by cutting the palm down, so he is telling them to cut the trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life example of the ״רק״ rule: the less valuable tree is cut to save the more valuable plant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Date palms that harm more valuable grapevines may be cut down.

steps.title: רב חסדא uproots palms growing among vines
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא had palms removed from among his vines, reasoning that vines are worth more than palms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא saw date palms among grapevines. He told his sharecropper: "Uproot them. Vines can buy palms, but palms cannot buy vines."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, similar story. רב חסדא spells out the reason clearly: vines are worth more than palms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Vines can buy palms" is a way of saying that vines are more valuable. It is worth giving up the palms to protect the vines. This gives the value-based reasoning behind ״רק״ in plain words.

keyTerms.meaning: Can buy (here: are worth more than)

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא חֲזָא תָּאלֵי בֵּי גוּפְנֵי.
phrases.english: Rav Chisda saw date palms among the grapevines.
He said to his sharecropper: Uproot them;
vines can buy palms,
palms cannot buy vines.
phrases.notes: In other words, vines are worth more money than palms.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא חֲזָא תָּאלֵי בֵּי גוּפְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to שמואל's, now with the reason stated outright.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Less valuable palms are uprooted to protect more valuable vines.
steps.whatToRemember: Value decides: a less valuable tree may be cut down to protect a more valuable one, as the stories of שמואל and רב חסדא show.

steps.title: Paying is not enough; he must ask forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that someone who injured another is not forgiven until he asks the victim, even after paying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though he pays the victim, he is not forgiven until he asks him for forgiveness. As it says: "Now return the wife" and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that paying money for an injury does not finish the matter; the one who caused it must also ask the victim to forgive him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money covers the damage, but the wrong done to the person still needs his forgiveness. The proof is אבימלך: even after he returned שרה, he still needed אברהם to pray for him, so making things right included making peace with the person he wronged.

keyTerms.meaning: "As it says": brings a פסוק as the source

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the payment is optional or that asking forgiveness replaces it. The משנה requires both: paying AND asking forgiveness.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לוֹ,
phrases.english: Even though he gives him the payment,
he is not forgiven
until he asks him for forgiveness.
As it says: "Now return the wife" and so on.
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:7. The rest of the פסוק says אברהם will pray for אבימלך.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לוֹ, אֵין נִמְחָל לוֹ עַד שֶׁיְּבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a new משנה about forgiveness after an injury.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who caused an injury is not forgiven until he asks the victim, even after paying in full.
steps.whyThisMatters: Repairing a wrong against another person has two parts: paying for the harm and making peace with the person.

steps.title: What is the source that refusing to forgive is cruel?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks for the source that a victim who will not forgive is called cruel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that if he does not forgive him, he is cruel?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns to the victim's side and asks for a source. This step sets up the next one, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After teaching that the one who caused harm must ask, the משנה adds a matching duty on the victim. The victim should not hold back forgiveness once he is asked.

keyTerms.meaning: "And from where": a request for a source

phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he does not forgive him,
that he is cruel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם לֹא מָחַל לוֹ, שֶׁהוּא אַכְזָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the duty of the one who caused harm to the duty of the victim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that refusing to forgive is cruel.

steps.title: אברהם prayed for אבימלך
steps.stepSummary: The source is that אברהם prayed for אבימלך and he was healed. The victim forgave and even prayed for the one who wronged him.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And אברהם prayed to God, and God healed אבימלך" and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question with a פסוק. אברהם, the one who was wronged, prayed for אבימלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם did not hold a grudge once אבימלך made things right; he prayed for him. That sets the standard: a victim who refuses to forgive falls short of it and is called cruel.
steps.whatToRemember: The one who caused harm must pay AND ask forgiveness. The victim, once asked, should forgive like אברהם did; refusing is called cruel.

phrases.english: As it says: "And Abraham prayed to God,
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:17

phrases.english: and God healed Abimelech" and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אברהם prayed for אבימלך, showing that the victim should forgive and not be cruel.

steps.title: Permission to injure the body does not exempt the injurer
steps.stepSummary: If a person tells someone to blind his eye, cut off his hand, or break his leg, the one who does it is חייב. This is true even if he was told he would be פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'Blind my eye,' 'Cut off my hand,' or 'Break my leg,' the one who does it must pay. Even if he said 'on condition that you are exempt,' he must still pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules that hurting someone's body is never made free of payment, even when the victim asked for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally permission sounds like it should remove blame. But for injuries to the body, the משנה says the injurer is חייב both when the victim simply asked and when he explicitly promised to exempt him. The משנה here states the rule without giving a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that you will be exempt

phrases.english: One who says: 'Blind my eye';
'Cut off my hand';
'Break my leg' — he is liable.
'On condition that you are exempt' — he is still liable.
phrases.notes: Even when the victim clearly said 'you won't have to pay,' the injurer still has to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה about one who injures another, now adding the case where the victim gave permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For injury to the body, the injurer is חייב even with permission and even with an explicit exemption.

steps.title: Permission to damage property exempts only if stated clearly
steps.stepSummary: If someone says 'tear my garment' or 'break my jug,' the one who does it is חייב. But if he said 'on condition that you are exempt,' the one who does it is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'Tear my garment' or 'Break my jug,' the one who does it must pay. If he said 'on condition that you are exempt,' the one who does it does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns to damage to property and gives a different rule than for the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With property, a plain request to damage is not enough to exempt the damager, and he is still חייב. But if the owner clearly gave up his right to payment, the damager is פטור. This is the difference from step 7, where even an explicit exemption did not help for injury to the body.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. For the body, the damager is חייב even with an explicit exemption. For property, the explicit exemption works.

phrases.english: 'Tear my garment';
'Break my jug' — he is liable.
'On condition that you are exempt' — he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a contrast with step 7: property is treated differently from the body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For property, a plain request leaves the damager חייב, but an explicit exemption makes him פטור.

steps.title: No one can permit damage to someone else
steps.stepSummary: If someone says 'do this to so-and-so, and you will be exempt,' the one who does it is חייב. This is true whether he hurts that person's body or damages his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'Do this to So-and-so, on condition that you are exempt,' the one who does it must pay, whether he hurt the person himself or his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by ruling that permission given by a third person does not help at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the owner can give up his own money. A person who gives permission to hurt someone else is giving away something that is not his. So the damager is חייב in every case, for the body or for property.
steps.whatToRemember: Body: always חייב, even with an explicit exemption. Property: פטור only with an explicit exemption. Someone else's body or property: always חייב.

phrases.english: 'Do so to So-and-so
on condition that you are exempt' — he is liable,
whether to his body or to his property.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עֲשֵׂה כֵּן לְאִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי עַל מְנָת לִפְטוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case and closes the משנה's list of permission cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Permission from a third person never exempts the damager, for the body or for property.

steps.title: Money pays for embarrassment, but hurt needs forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the fixed sums are payment for בושת. For the צער caused to the victim, no amount of offerings brings forgiveness until the injurer asks the victim, as the פסוק says about אבימלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: All the amounts mentioned are payment for embarrassment. But for his pain, even if the injurer brought all the finest rams in the world, he is not forgiven until he asks the victim, as it says: 'Return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה's earlier rule that paying does not bring forgiveness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא separates two things. The money is a set payment for the בושת. The צער caused to the person is not wiped away by any payment or קרבן; only asking the victim brings forgiveness. The proof is that אבימלך had to go back to אברהם himself, and אברהם prayed for him.

keyTerms.meaning: His pain, the hurt done to him
The rams of נביות, the finest offerings

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that money alone does not repair hurting a person. One must also ask for forgiveness.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
All these amounts that they said are payment for his embarrassment;
phrases.notes: These are the set sums from the earlier משנה for embarrassing someone.

phrases.english: but for his pain,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הֵבִיא כׇּל אֵילֵי נְבָיוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: even if he brought all the rams of Nebaioth in the world,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 60:7

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נִמְחָל לוֹ עַד שֶׁיְּבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: he is not forgiven until he asks the victim.
As it says: 'Return the man's wife,
for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by explaining the משנה's rule (step 4) that payment does not bring forgiveness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment covers בושת, but forgiveness for the hurt requires asking the victim, learned from אבימלך and אברהם.

steps.title: Must only a prophet's wife be returned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the פסוק just quoted. It says 'return the wife, for he is a prophet.' Does that mean only a prophet's wife must be returned, and not anyone else's?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean a prophet's wife has to be returned, but another man's wife does not have to be returned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the quoted פסוק sounds, setting up an explanation of its wording in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for he is a prophet' seem to give the reason for returning the wife. That would wrongly suggest that a regular man's wife need not be returned. The גמרא raises this problem so it can explain what the phrase really means.

phrases.english: So a prophet's wife needs to be returned,
but another man's wife does not need to be returned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'כי נביא הוא' in the פסוק from בראשית 20:7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason for returning her is that her husband is a prophet, the פסוק seems to suggest a regular man's wife need not be returned, which cannot be right.

steps.title: Return any man's wife, not only a prophet's
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the name of רבי יונתן answers that 'return the man's wife' applies in every case, whether or not the husband is a נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: 'Return the man's wife' means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 11. The command to return the wife stands on its own and applies to every married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that 'for he is a prophet' was the reason for returning שרה. רבי יונתן separates the two parts of the פסוק. 'Return the man's wife' is a general rule, and 'he is a prophet' answers something else, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case / no matter what

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'for he is a prophet' as the reason she must be returned. According to this answer, every wife must be returned. The prophet part answers a different claim.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said
Rabbi Yonatan said:
"Return the man's wife" — in any case.
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:7. He means you must give her back no matter who the husband is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק: the two clauses are separate statements.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to say a wife is returned only because her husband is a prophet.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every man's wife must be returned. 'He is a prophet' serves a different purpose.

steps.title: Why אבימלך's excuse fails: אברהם was a prophet and understood the danger
steps.stepSummary: אבימלך claimed he was innocent because אברהם and שרה called themselves brother and sister. The reply: אברהם was a נביא and saw that this town asked guests about their wives instead of feeding them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for what you said, 'Will You kill even a righteous nation? Didn't he tell me she is his sister, and she said he is her brother?' He is a prophet and already understood: when a guest comes to town, do people ask him about food and drink, or about his wife, 'Is she your wife? Is she your sister?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the words 'for he is a prophet.' They answer אבימלך's claim that he did nothing wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימלך blamed אברהם for hiding that שרה was his wife. The reply is that אברהם, being a נביא, read the situation correctly. A town that asks a guest about his wife before offering him food is a dangerous place. So אבימלך's people caused the problem, and אבימלך is not as innocent as he claims.

keyTerms.meaning: Will You kill even a righteous nation? (אבימלך's complaint)
A guest / traveler staying in a town
Matters of / things having to do with

phrases.english: And as for what you said:
phrases.notes: "You" is אבימלך. The גמרא is answering him directly.

phrases.english: "Will You kill even a righteous nation?!"
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:4–5

phrases.aramaic: הֲלֹא הוּא אָמַר לִי אֲחֹתִי הִיא,
phrases.english: Did he not tell me 'She is my sister,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא גַּם הִיא אָמְרָה אָחִי הוּא!״
phrases.english: and she, she too, said 'He is my brother'!"
He is a prophet, and he already learned [the lesson]:
A guest who comes to town —

phrases.aramaic: עַל עִסְקֵי אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה שׁוֹאֲלִין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: do people ask him about matters of eating and drinking,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ עַל עִסְקֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ שׁוֹאֲלִין אוֹתוֹ –
phrases.english: or do they ask him about matters of his wife —
"Is she your wife?" "Is she your sister?"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from Step 12 by explaining what 'for he is a prophet' is doing in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the purpose of the extra clause in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'For he is a prophet' looked like the reason the wife had to be returned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words answer אבימלך's excuse: אברהם, as a נביא, saw the danger, so אבימלך is to blame.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the next step's rule that someone is held responsible for what he should have known.

steps.title: A בן נח is punished for failing to learn
steps.stepSummary: From אבימלך's case the גמרא learns that a בן נח can be put to death even when he did not know, because he should have learned and did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn that a בן נח is put to death, because he should have learned and did not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a law from the אבימלך story. Not knowing does not excuse a בן נח when he should have learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימלך said he was innocent because he didn't know שרה was married. The גמרא answered that he and his people should have behaved properly, and then the danger would not have existed. This becomes a general rule: for a בן נח, failing to learn is itself his fault, so he is held liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew, who is bound by the seven מצוות of the children of נח

steps.whatToRemember: A בן נח cannot claim 'I didn't know' as an excuse, because he was supposed to learn.

phrases.english: From here [we learn] that a בן נח is put to death,
phrases.notes: He means: even when he sinned without knowing it was forbidden.

phrases.english: since he should have learned and did not learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Derives a general law from the reply to אבימלך in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן נח is liable to death even without knowing, because he should have learned.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר explains the double word 'closed up'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'עצור עצר', with the verb doubled. רבי אלעזר explains that the men were closed in one way (semen) and the women in two ways (semen and birth).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For the Lord had closed up [doubly].' רבי אלעזר said: Why these two closings? One for a man, semen. Two for a woman, semen and giving birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another פסוק in the same story and asks why the word for 'closing up' is written twice. רבי אלעזר asks the question and gives the answer himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A doubled word in a פסוק suggests more than one meaning. רבי אלעזר says the punishment hit men and women differently. The men could not emit semen, and the women could neither emit semen nor give birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Closed up (the verb is written twice)

phrases.english: "For the Lord had closed up [doubly]" —
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:18

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Why these two closings?
One for a man — semen,
two for a woman — semen and giving birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כִּי עָצֹר עָצַר ה׳״ – אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain another פסוק from the same אבימלך story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubled verb means one blockage for men (semen) and two for women (semen and birth).

steps.title: A ברייתא counts more blockages
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the doubled word more broadly. Men were blocked in two ways (semen and urine), and women in three (semen, urine, and birth).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: Two for a man, semen and urine. Three for a woman, semen, urine, and birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the same doubled word differently from רבי אלעזר. It adds one more blockage for both men and women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר counted one blockage for men and two for women. The ברייתא adds urine for both, so it counts two for men and three for women. It is a fuller reading of the same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא (a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: The doubled 'עצור עצר' is read as more than one blockage. רבי אלעזר counts 1 for men and 2 for women. The ברייתא counts 2 for men and 3 for women.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
Two for a man — semen and urine,
three for a woman —
semen, urine, and giving birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a broader reading of the same doubled word that רבי אלעזר explained in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Men were blocked in two ways (semen and urine), and women in three (semen, urine, and birth).

steps.title: רבינא's widest reading of the blockage
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the men of אבימלך's house were blocked in three ways and the women in four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Three blockages in a man: semen, urine, and the anus. Four in a woman: semen, birth, urine, and the anus.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a third and even broader reading of the doubled word 'עצור עצר'. He adds that the people could not empty their bowels either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר counted one blockage for men and two for women. The ברייתא added urine, making two and three. רבינא adds the anus, making three for men and four for women, so the people could not relieve themselves at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'small ones'; here it means urine (the 'small needs')
Literally 'mouth of the ring'; the anus

steps.whatToRemember: There are three growing readings of 'עצור עצר': רבי אלעזר (1 and 2), the ברייתא (2 and 3), and רבינא (3 and 4).

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Three in a man:
semen, urine, and the anus;
four in a woman:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע וְלֵידָה וּקְטַנִּים וּפִי טַבַּעַת.
phrases.english: semen, birth, urine, and the anus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, broader reading of the same doubled verb, after רבי אלעזר and the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubled verb teaches three blockages for men (semen, urine, anus) and four for women (semen, birth, urine, anus).

steps.title: Even the hens could not lay eggs
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי reads 'every womb' as including animals: even אבימלך's hen could not lay its egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every womb' — the school of רבי ינאי said: Even a hen of אבימלך's house did not lay its egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at another word in the same פסוק, 'כל רחם' (every womb). The school of רבי ינאי says the plague reached even the chickens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כל' (every) is read as including more than just the people. So the blockage covered every living thing in the household, even a hen laying eggs.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Every womb'; words from the פסוק about אבימלך's household

phrases.english: 'Every womb' —
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:18

phrases.english: the school of Rabbi Yannai said:
Even a hen of Avimelech's house
did not lay its egg.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בְּעַד כׇּל רֶחֶם״ – אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the doubled verb to the next words in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Every womb' includes even animals: the hens of אבימלך's house could not lay eggs.

steps.title: רבא asks for the source of a known rule about prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רבה בר מרי where we learn that someone who prays for a friend, while needing the same thing, is answered first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מרי: Where do we learn what the Rabbis said: Anyone who asks for mercy for his friend, and he needs that same thing, is answered first?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic with a question. He wants a פסוק behind a known teaching of the Rabbis about prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is: if you pray for someone else's need while you have that same need, ה׳ answers you first. רבא is not doubting the rule; he only wants its source. This is linked to the story of אבימלך, which will be the answer in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Where is this matter learned from?
One who asks for mercy; one who prays
The אמורא whom רבא is asking; he answers each of רבא's questions

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabba bar Mari:
Where do we learn this matter that the Rabbis said:
Anyone who asks for mercy for his friend
and he himself needs that same thing,
he is answered first?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי: מְנַָא הָא מִילְּתָא דַאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, connected to the אבימלך story through the answer that will follow.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that is the source for the rule that one who prays for a friend while needing the same thing is answered first.

steps.title: רבה בר מרי brings a proof from איוב
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי answers from the פסוק that ה׳ restored איוב's fortune when he prayed for his friends.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it is written, 'And ה׳ restored איוב's fortune when he prayed for his friends.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי answers רבא's question with a פסוק from the book of איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב himself had lost everything and needed help. He prayed for his friends, and at that moment his own fortune was restored. That shows that praying for others brought his own answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Restored the fortune (brought back what was lost)

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is written:
'And ה׳ restored the fortune of Iyov
phrases.notes: איוב 42:10

phrases.english: when he prayed for his friends.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַה׳ שָׁב אֶת שְׁבוּת אִיּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question with a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is איוב 42:10: איוב's fortune was restored when he prayed for his friends.

steps.title: רבא's own proof from אברהם and אבימלך
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a different source: אברהם prayed for אבימלך's household to have children, and right after that שרה was remembered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You learn it from there, and I learn it from here: 'And אברהם prayed to God, and God healed אבימלך, his wife, and his maidservants,' and right after it is written, 'And ה׳ remembered שרה as He said,' meaning: as אברהם said about אבימלך.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own source for the same rule. He takes it from the story of אבימלך that the גמרא has been discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם prayed that אבימלך's household could have children again, while he and שרה still had no child. Right after that, the תורה says שרה was remembered and had a child. רבא reads 'as He said' as 'as אברהם said for אבימלך', so the very thing אברהם prayed for others was given to him.

keyTerms.meaning: And I say it from here

steps.whatToRemember: One who prays for a friend while needing the same thing is answered first. רבה בר מרי learns it from איוב; רבא learns it from אברהם praying for אבימלך and then שרה having a child.

phrases.english: He said to him: You say it from there,
and I say it from here:
'And Avraham prayed to God,
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:17

phrases.english: and God healed Avimelech
and his wife and his maidservants, etc.',
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'etc.', is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And ה׳ remembered Sarah
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:1, which comes right after the story of אבימלך.

phrases.english: as He said, etc.' —
as Avraham said for Avimelech.
phrases.notes: רבא reads 'as he said' as pointing back to what אברהם said in his prayer for אבימלך.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ מֵהָתָם, וַאֲנָא אָמֵינָא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the same rule instead of רבה בר מרי's source from איוב.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who prays for a friend while needing the same thing is answered first.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 20:17 followed by 21:1: אברהם prayed for אבימלך's household to have children, and then שרה was remembered, 'as אברהם said for אבימלך'.

steps.title: Source for the saying 'the cabbage is struck with the thorn'
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רבה בר מרי for a פסוק behind the popular saying that the cabbage gets hit along with the thorn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מרי: Where do we learn the thing people say, 'Together with the thorn, the cabbage gets struck'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks for the source of a folk saying. The idea is that a good person near bad people can suffer along with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another question in the same style as the earlier one in Step 19. רבא takes a common saying and asks where the תנ״ך hints to it. The answer will come in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabba bar Mari:
From where is this matter derived
that people say:
Together with the thorn, the cabbage gets struck?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in the same series as Step 19, asking for a source for another popular saying.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that innocent people can suffer together with the guilty.

steps.title: Answer from ירמיהו: 'You all have transgressed'
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי brings a פסוק from ירמיהו where ה׳ says 'all of you' sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it is written, 'Why will you argue with Me? All of you have sinned against Me, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי answers רבא's question with a פסוק from ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'all of you' groups everyone together, including people who did not sin. That matches the saying: the innocent cabbage gets hit along with the guilty thorn.

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is written:
"Why will you contend with Me?
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:29

phrases.english: You all have transgressed against Me, says ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ירמיהו 2:29, where 'all of you' includes the innocent together with the sinners.

steps.title: רבא's source from the תורה: 'How long will you refuse'
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a source from the תורה instead: ה׳'s words to משה after the מן was gathered on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You bring it from there, and I bring it from here: 'How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and My teachings?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own source for the same saying, this time from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like in Step 21, רבא prefers a source from the תורה over one from נביאים‎. ה׳ says 'you' in the plural to משה, so even משה, who did not sin, is grouped with the people who gathered מן on שבת.

phrases.english: He said to him: You say it from there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means a פסוק in נביאים. 'Here' will be a פסוק in the תורה.

phrases.english: and I say it from here:
"How long will you refuse
phrases.notes: שמות 16:28. ה׳ says this to משה after people gathered מן on שבת.

phrases.english: to keep My commandments and My teachings?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ מֵהָתָם, וַאֲנָא אָמֵינָא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different, earlier source for the same idea answered in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The saying that the innocent suffer together with the guilty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 16:28, said in the plural to משה, which includes even משה with those who sinned.
steps.whatToRemember: Two sources show that innocent people can get caught up with sinners: ירמיהו ('all of you sinned') and, as רבא prefers, the תורה ('how long will you refuse,' said to משה).

steps.title: Who were the five brothers יוסף brought to פרעה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רבה בר מרי which five brothers יוסף presented to פרעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מרי: It is written, 'And from among his brothers he took five men.' Who are these five?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question about a פסוק: which five of the brothers did יוסף bring to פרעה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'five' but does not give names. רבא wants to know exactly who they were.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי: כְּתִיב:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabba bar Mari: It is written:
"And from among his brothers
he took five men" —
phrases.notes: בראשית 47:2. יוסף brings these brothers to meet פרעה.

phrases.english: Who are these five?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated question from רבא to רבה בר מרי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the five brothers in בראשית 47:2.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the brothers whose names were doubled
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי quotes רבי יוחנן: the five are the tribes whose names appear twice in משה's ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: Those whose names were doubled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי answers with a teaching of רבי יוחנן that identifies the five brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן points to משה's ברכות at the end of the תורה. The tribes whose names are mentioned twice there are the five יוסף brought to פרעה. These were understood to be the weaker brothers.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
Those whose names were doubled.
phrases.notes: This refers to משה's ברכות in דברים 33, where some tribes' names show up twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The five are the tribes whose names are repeated in משה's ברכות.

steps.title: But יהודה's name was doubled too
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer: יהודה's name is also doubled, so the rule seems to include him.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה's name was also doubled!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the answer from רבי יוחנן by pointing out that יהודה's name is also repeated, even though יהודה was not one of the weak brothers. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a doubled name marks one of the five weak brothers יוסף presented, then יהודה should be among them. But יהודה was strong, so a doubled name cannot be the sign. This undercuts the identification from רבי יוחנן, and step 28 answers it.

phrases.english: Judah too
had his name doubled!
phrases.notes: יהודה's name also appears twice in משה's ברכה, so the rule seems to include him too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification given in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that the five are those whose names were doubled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יהודה's name is also doubled, yet he was strong and not one of the weak brothers, so a doubled name cannot be what marks the five.

steps.title: יהודה's name was doubled for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי answers that יהודה's name is repeated for his own matter, and brings a question of רבי יונתן on the פסוקים of ראובן and יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: יהודה's name was doubled because of his own story. As רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'Let ראובן live and not die, and may his men be few,' followed by 'And this for יהודה'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי defends רבי יוחנן's rule by saying יהודה's doubled name has a separate explanation. He starts by bringing a question on why the ברכה of יהודה is joined to the ברכה of ראובן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 27 was that יהודה's name is doubled, so the rule should include him among the five weak brothers. The answer is that his name is doubled for a different reason, so the rule does not apply to him. The question on the פסוק prepares the story that explains that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: for his own matter, for his own reason
what is the meaning of what is written
and this for יהודה (the start of יהודה's ברכה)

phrases.english: He said to him: It was doubled for his own matter.
phrases.notes: He means יהודה's name is repeated for a separate reason, so it doesn't make him one of the five weak brothers.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Let Reuven live and not die,
phrases.notes: דברים 33:6-7

phrases.english: and may his men be few" —
"And this for Yehuda"?
phrases.notes: The question is why יהודה's ברכה is linked to ראובן's with the word 'and.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27 against רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason for the same textual feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every tribe whose name is doubled was one of the five weak brothers, so יהודה should be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהודה's name is doubled for his own special story, so the rule does not include him.

steps.title: משה prays for יהודה because he led ראובן to confess
steps.stepSummary: יהודה's bones rolled in their coffin for forty years until משה asked for mercy, pointing out that יהודה caused ראובן to confess.
steps.simpleTranslation: All forty years that ישראל were in the desert, יהודה's bones were rolling around in the coffin. Then משה asked for mercy and said: Master of the world, who caused ראובן to confess? יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי יונתן's explanation of why יהודה's ברכה comes right after ראובן's. משה argued that יהודה deserved mercy because his confession led ראובן to confess too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link between the two ברכות is the theme of confessing. ראובן is blessed to live, and יהודה, who inspired that confession, should be helped as well. This explains the 'and' that joins their ברכות.

phrases.english: All those forty years
that Israel were in the desert,
the bones of Yehuda were
rolling around in the coffin;
until Moshe came and asked for mercy —
he said before Him: Master of the world,
who caused Reuven to confess?
Yehuda!
phrases.notes: ראובן saw יהודה admit his wrongdoing, and that led ראובן to admit his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל אוֹתָן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יונתן's question from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהודה's ברכה is joined to ראובן's because יהודה caused ראובן to confess, and משה used this to ask for mercy for יהודה.

steps.title: Each phrase of יהודה's ברכה fixes one more problem
steps.stepSummary: Each part of the פסוק is read as a separate prayer by משה that fixed a separate problem for יהודה, until he was fully restored. This is why his name appears again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, 'Hear, ה׳, the voice of יהודה' — his bones went back into their sockets. But they still did not bring him up to the yeshiva in heaven, so: 'And bring him to his people.' He still did not understand what the רבנן were saying and could not discuss and argue with them, so: 'His hands will fight for him.' He still could not reach conclusions that matched the הלכה, so: 'And You will be a help against his enemies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through יהודה's ברכה phrase by phrase. Each phrase is an answer to one more problem יהודה still had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order goes from the body (his bones), to a place (entering the heavenly yeshiva), to learning (following the discussion), and finally to reaching the right הלכה. Because his ברכה is a special prayer about his own story, his name appears again for that reason. So the doubled name does not mean he was weak.

keyTerms.meaning: into its socket, into its place

steps.whatToRemember: יהודה's name is doubled because of משה's special prayer for him, not because he was weak. So רבי יוחנן's rule about the five brothers still stands.

phrases.english: Immediately: "Hear, ה׳, the voice of Yehuda" —
phrases.notes: דברים 33:7

phrases.english: his limbs went back into their sockets.
They still were not bringing him up
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected text.

phrases.english: to the yeshiva in heaven,
so: "And bring him to his people."

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה יָדַע מַאי קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: He did not know what the Rabbis were saying,
or how to discuss and argue with the Rabbis,
so: "His hands will fight for him."
His learning still did not come out right for him
in line with the halacha,
so: "And You will be a help against his enemies."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 29, showing what משה's prayer brought about step by step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each phrase of יהודה's ברכה is a prayer that fixed another problem, until יהודה was fully restored.

steps.title: Where do we learn 'poverty follows the poor'?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רבה בר מרי for a source for the popular saying that poverty follows poor people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מרי: Where does the thing people say come from: 'Poverty follows the poor'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his series of questions to רבה בר מרי, asking for a source for a well-known folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic in the same list of sayings that רבא asks about. The saying means that a poor person keeps losing even more, because bad luck follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: where does this matter come from

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי,
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabba bar Mari:
From where is this matter
that people say:
Poverty follows the poor person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new saying in רבא's series of questions to רבה בר מרי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the saying 'poverty follows the poor.'

steps.title: The proof from the בכורים baskets
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי brings a משנה: the rich bring בכורים in gold and silver baskets, the poor in willow baskets, and the baskets are given to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As we learned in a משנה: Rich people bring בכורים in baskets of gold and silver, and poor people bring them in woven baskets of peeled willow. The baskets and the בכורים are given to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי answers with a משנה about how people bring בכורים to the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor person gives away his basket together with his fruit, while the rich person gets his expensive basket back. So the one who has less loses even more, which shows poverty follows the poor.

keyTerms.meaning: first fruits brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: He said to him: As we learned in a Mishna:
phrases.notes: בכורים 3:8

phrases.english: Rich people bring first fruits
in baskets of gold and of silver,
and poor people in woven baskets
of peeled willow.
The baskets and the first fruits are given to the Kohanim.
phrases.notes: This is about the poor people's baskets. They lose them, while the rich get their gold and silver ones back.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the rich give away their gold baskets. The point is the opposite: only the poor lose their baskets.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question in step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה of בכורים, where the poor give away their baskets but the rich keep theirs.

steps.title: רבא prepares his own proof from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא says: You brought the proof from there, but I bring it from here, which introduces his own source.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You say it from there, and I say it from here:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts that there is a proof, but says he has a different source. This line is only setting up the next move, where he will bring his own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like in step 24, רבא prefers an earlier source from the תורה over the משנה that רבה בר מרי brought. The actual פסוק comes on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: He said to him: You say it from there,
and I say it from here:
